title: Freewheeling Galaxies Collide in a Blaze of Star Birth (NGC 1275)
caption: Colliding galaxies in NGC 1275, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1275, Perseus A, 3C 84 · constellation Perseus · about About 235 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: M. Donahue (STScI) and J. Trauger (JPL)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A dusty spiral galaxy, seen nearly edge-on, appears to spin like a pinwheel while gliding through the larger, bright galaxy NGC 1275. Traces of spiral structure, heavy dust lanes and bright blue patches of active star formation mark the foreground system. NGC 1275 lies about 235 million light-years away in Perseus, at the center of the large Perseus Cluster of galaxies.

The galaxy behind is a giant elliptical with faint, peculiar spiral structure in its nucleus. They are believed to be crashing together at over 6 million miles per hour. The crash is making gas and dust already in the bright galaxy swirl toward its center, and X-ray and radio emission from NGC 1275 point to a probable black hole there.

The encounter, which may draw in a few smaller galaxies besides the main pair, is also producing new stars and large star clusters. These clusters resemble the Milky Way's old globular clusters in shape but are far younger, each holding 100,000 to a million stars.

understand.summary: Built from blue, red and infrared observations with Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2. The color mapping is not published.
understand.eye: Part of the data is infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the exposures total about 4 hours.

explore: Outside the frame, NGC 1275 shows intricate filaments on a much larger scale, a typical feature of bright galaxies at the centers of clusters. The color picture combines archived blue and red Hubble data from 1995 by John Trauger and Jon Holtzman with infrared follow-up observations made in 2001 for the Hubble Heritage project.
